newsitem.title: UK: Oil rally takes a breather but bullishness lingers.
newsitem.headline: Oil rally takes a breather but bullishness lingers.

text.p: A torrid rally which has taken oil prices as much as $9 a barrel over last year's levels paused for breath on Monday but bullish sentiment remains, traders said.
At 1655 GMT, London December futures for international benchmark Brent crude stood up one cent on the day at $24.53 recovering slightly from the day's low of $24.38.
Traders had expected a modest retracement following Friday's moderate gains. Brent last week hit a post-Gulf War high of $25.06.
The prolonged rally, sparked by strong demand, tensions in oil producing centres Middle East and Russia and low heating fuel stocks ahead of the winter, has added $7 to oil prices since mid-June.
U.S. heating oil stocks are down 27 percent against the same time last year with key East Coast inventories off a huge 43 percent, the Department of Energy said last week.

Meanwhile, European inventories of middle distillate including heating oil and jet fuel are running some 10.6 percent below year-earlier levels even though refineries on both sides of the Atlantic are running flat out to build stocks.
"There is a quite fantastic incentive (to maximize heating oil output)," said Geoff Pyne, energy economist at UBS in London.
